inferences: Unspecified input normalization implemented as RGB [0,1], bilinear resizing; no ImageNet pretrained backbone.
Scale branches have independent PTC and positional embedding parameters; LN over channels.
Use sequence-summed CTC for batch size one, avoiding implicit target-length rescaling.
Convolution BN/ReLU and first-in-pair pooling follow assigned Table 2.
Pinned PHOENIX evaluator mirror and SCTK implement benchmark scoring; original author evaluator remains unavailable.

The training CSV contains 5672 examples; exactly one pinned known-broken clip was excluded with approval, leaving 5671 usable examples matching the training reference. Exact unchanged dev/test reference coverage is required.
Learning-rate halving at epochs 45, 50 and 55 is one reading of the paper's "After 40 epochs, we decay the learning rate by 0.5 every 5 epochs"; 40/45/50/55 and 41/46/51/56 are also possible.

Batch size one makes every BatchNorm layer use single-video statistics in training, including temporal layers over one sequence; stored running statistics then mismatch evaluation (quantified by bn-generalization-diagnostic-2).

Summed CTC makes the data gradient roughly 11.7 times larger relative to the L2 term than PyTorch's default target-length-normalized reduction (about 11.7 glosses per sentence from the paper's corpus figures). Coupled weight_decay adds lambda*W, whereas equation 15 implies 2*lambda*W. The authors' reduction is unknown.
BatchNorm after the temporal convolutions follows the cited FCN paper ("added after every convolutional layer"); random initialization follows FCN ("end-to-end trainable without any pre-training").
